taxonomy.definition: The right to hold the office of archon.
The right to serve as general or in high-level military leadership.
The right to serve as a juror or heliast in law courts.
The right to sit on a deliberative body such as the Boule or Senate.
The right to hold a royal or monarchical office.
The power to participate in the governing decisions or self-regulation of a community.
The right of a sub-polity or city-state to manage its own internal affairs under a larger power.
The right to have a case heard in court before punishment or seizure.
The right to bring suits in specific venues like maritime, commercial, or local courts.
Freedom from being detained without legal cause or prior to trial.
The status of being a legal member of the body politic, including the right to retain such status.
The right to be registered in local or kinship groups like demes or wards.
The right to keep one's possessions, land, and the income derived from them.
Freedom from having property confiscated by the state or creditors.
The right not to be struck or physically abused by another private individual.
Exemption from the use of torture to extract evidence during legal proceedings.
Exemption from physical beating or restraint as a state-sanctioned penalty.
The right to be free from being sold or bound into slavery due to unpaid financial obligations.
The general right to be free from bondage or the status of a slave.
The right to choose or refuse a spouse without external compulsion.
Autonomy from official oversight regarding domestic habits or personal conduct.
The right to receive state funds, distributions, or maintenance.
The right to receive awards, crowns, or special seating for service.
The right to participate in public messes or dining in the Town Hall (Prytaneum).
The right not to be executed by the state.
The right to a trial before a death sentence is carried out.

taxonomy.parent_meta: Right to vote in the Ekklesia
taxonomy.definition: The right to cast a vote on legislation or motions in the popular assembly.

taxonomy.parent_meta: Right to vote in the Ekklesia
taxonomy.definition: The right to vote for candidates for public office.
Freedom from the obligation to fund public services like the trierarchy or chorus.
The right of an individual (including slaves in some cases) to keep the pay from their labor.
The right to conduct trade, charge fees, or practice an art for profit.
The right to join in sacrifices, festivals, and communal worship.
The right to enter temples or purified precincts.
The right to stand on the platform and address the popular assembly.
The right to introduce a formal motion or decree (psephisma).
The right to succeed to an estate through lineage or law.

taxonomy.right: Right to a share of an estate
taxonomy.definition: The right for children or heirs to receive a portion of the family wealth.

taxonomy.right: Pay for assembly or jury service
taxonomy.definition: The right to receive a daily wage for participating in the assembly or courts.
The right to subsistence pay for the infirm or impoverished.

taxonomy.parent_meta: Right to reside in the city
taxonomy.definition: The right to live within the borders of the city or territory.

taxonomy.parent_meta: Right to reside in the city
taxonomy.definition: The right to enter the market and public square.
Exemption from being sued or tried for actions taken, often while in office.
Freedom from paying income, war, or alien (metic) taxes.

taxonomy.right: Exemption from manual or agricultural labor
taxonomy.definition: Freedom from being forced into physical toil or state-mandated labor.
Freedom from the obligation to serve in the army or navy.
The right to use gymnasia or engage in general athletics.
The right to receive schooling, whether academic, moral, or military.
The right to possess and acquire real estate/plots of land.
The general right to travel locally or abroad without restriction.
The right to own or keep weapons and military equipment.
The right to determine heirs and distribute wealth after death via a testament.
The right to seek redress for being insulted or libeled in public.
The right to form a legally recognized marriage with another citizen.
The right to receive or have provided a marriage portion.
Freedom from the requirement to account for official actions or finances (euthynai).
Freedom from being expelled from the city without a formal process like ostracism.
The right to give legal testimony or depositions.
The right to be buried at state expense or with state honors.
The right to legally adopt an heir or son.
